text:
Noah: Heads up from the embedding bring-up run — after applying our int8 path to ember-3, recall@1 dropped by ~5.8% on the semantic-sim holdout. FP32 r@1=0.688 -> INT8 r@1=0.648.
Ivy: Oof. Is that localized to any cohort? short vs medium vs long?
Noah: Medium-length (10-35 tokens) primarily. Short (<9) and ultra-long (>80) are stable.
Rohit: Could be directional rotation in the embedding space rather than norm collapse. Did you compare principal components pre/post quant?
Noah: Yes — ran PCA on a 10k sample. Top-3 eigenvectors show a measurable rotation. Procrustes alignment error ~0.027. Variance explained by PC1 changed from 0.17 -> 0.155.
Ivy: That level of rotation can flip edge neighbors. What's the topk-flip-rate?
Noah: top1-flip-rate ~12% for failing queries, top5-flip-rate ~28%. Most flips are swaps between rank 1/2 or 3/4, not random drifts.
Rohit: Share an example?
Noah: Pasted a trimmed example:
```
qid: 90021
fp32_top5: [(p_12,0.902),(p_5,0.896),(p_99,0.893),(p_44,0.887),(p_2,0.879)]
int8_top5: [(p_5,0.901),(p_12,0.895),(p_99,0.890),(p_44,0.886),(p_2,0.880)]
notes: top1/top2 swap, cos deltas ~0.005-0.01
```
Ivy: Looks like small scalar shifts. Did you check whitening/centering effects? We saw earlier that whitening can amplify small directional biases.
Noah: Ran with three preprocessing configs: none, mean-centering only, and full ZCA whitening. Results:
- FP32 (none) r@1=0.688
- INT8 (none) r@1=0.648
- FP32 (whiten) r@1=0.695
- INT8 (whiten) r@1=0.628
So whitening widened the gap.
Rohit: That implies quant bias interacts badly with whitening transform. Did you compare cosine-norm distributions?
Noah: Yes. Cosine norm (embedding normalized by L2 then cosine to cluster mean) shows mean shift +2.8% after quant, sd up slightly. Also QQ plot shows heavier tail on negatives.
Ivy: Try a few defensive quant configs: symmetric activations, per-channel act quant (if runtime supports), and KL calibration with 4k samples. Also rerun ONNX export with fuse_layernorm=false and with and without sqrt-scale fusion.
Noah: Queueing these permutations. My run matrix: 6 configs x 2 preprocessing modes x 3 cohorts. Command scaffold: 
```
./ci/embed_onboard.sh --model ember-3 --quant int8 --calib kl --calib-samples 4096 --act-quant symmetric --per-channel-acts --no-fuse-layernorm --preproc none,whiten --cohorts short,medium,long --out /tmp/ember3_quant_diag.log
```
jinx-bot: Job 5127 queued by Noah. ETA ~22m. Will post results to thread.
Rohit: Also compare FP16 baseline to ensure reduced mantissa alone isn't the issue. If FP16 matches FP32, it's a quantization scaling/bias problem.
Noah: Running FP16 now. Early FP16 sanity: r@1=0.687 (within noise). So mantissa loss isn't the culprit.
Ivy: Good. If KL+4k + symmetric acts recovers >3% we can ship a canary with that quant profile. If not, we should consider a short quant-aware finetune focusing on medium-length examples (2-3 epochs).
Rohit: One more ask: compute silhouette and cluster purity before/after for the medium cohort. That will tell us if neighborhood geometry is stretched.
Noah: Adding silhouette and purity to the next run and will provide small diffs + scatter of top-2 pairs for flipped queries. Also saving PCA rotation matrices for deeper analysis.
Ivy: Perfect. Thanks. Ping when the bot posts results. :eyes:
